title: Cohomology of $\PP^n$, Serre 1954
statement:
Let $k$ be a field, $X=\PP^n_k$, $\cO(m):=\cO_X(m)$, and
$S^m(V)$ the $m$-th symmetric power of $V=k^{n+1}$.

$$
H^0(X,\cO(m))=S^m(V)\ (m\ge0),\qquad
H^q(X,\cO(m))=0\ (q\notin\{0,n\}),
$$

$$
H^n(X,\cO(m))=0\ (m\ge-n),\qquad
H^n(X,\cO(m))=S^{-m-n-1}(V)^{\vee}\ (m\le-n-1),
$$

the two top-degree clauses for $n\ge1$; for $n=0$, $X=\Spec k$ and
every $\cO(m)$ is $\cO_X$, so $H^0(X,\cO(m))=k$ for all $m$ and there is
no higher cohomology. In particular (for all $n\ge0$)
$\omega_X=\cO_X(-n-1)$ and $H^q(X,\cO_X)=k\cdot\delta_{q,0}$.

proof.text: Apply [sk-thm-picard-pn] to the same field $k$, the same integer $n\ge0$, and the standard ordered coordinates of $X=\mathbf P^n_k$. Its statement contains this item verbatim: the degree-zero formula for $m\ge0$, vanishing for $q\notin\{0,n\}$, both top-degree formulas with the restriction $n\ge1$, the separate $n=0$ description for every integer $m$, the canonical-sheaf formula for all $n\ge0$, and the structure-sheaf cohomology consequence. Its conventions identify the twists with the standard glued twists, $H^q$ with Zariski module-sheaf cohomology, $S^r(k^{n+1})$ with homogeneous polynomials in these coordinates, and $\omega_X$ with $\Lambda^n\Omega^1_{X/k}$; thus no coefficient, duality, or canonical-sheaf comparison is being assumed. Forgetting its explanatory conventions paragraph leaves exactly the required assertions. No hypotheses are added and no case is dropped.
